key_insight: Citizen-led photovoltaic self-consumption stays viable mainly through collective coordination and fair allocation, while battery storage adds little value under today’s low surplus-remuneration market conditions.
engineering_relevance: For PV system design and community energy planning, the paper shows that governance and sharing strategy can matter more than adding hardware when electricity prices and export payments keep falling.
method: Analyzed high-resolution consumption data from a rural community with 24 users sharing one PV facility.
Compared static, dynamic, and hybrid energy-sharing models, both with and without storage.
Evaluated trade-offs among efficiency, fairness, investment cost, and governance complexity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that collective self-consumption lowers required PV capacity and investment cost, increases annual savings versus individual systems, and that battery storage is only attractive under specific market conditions.
watch_item: Results depend on current market rules and local consumption patterns, so conclusions may shift if electricity prices, surplus remuneration, or participation behavior change.
paper_title: Decision-support strategies for photovoltaic self-consumption under declining electricity prices and limited remuneration of surplus generation
